title: Canada Issues First-Ever Express Entry Draw for Skilled Military Recruits
excerpt: IRCC selected four foreign military personnel for permanent residence under a new category launched in February, marking the smallest Express Entry draw in history.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Canada's first Express Entry draw for military recruits issued only four invitations.
  • Minimum CRS score for military recruits was 368, significantly lower than typical scores.
  • Candidates must have 10 years of military service and a job offer from the Canadian Armed Forces.
  • In 2026, IRCC conducted 42 Express Entry draws, issuing over 104,000 invitations across all categories.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada conducted the first-ever Express Entry draw targeting skilled military recruits on July 23, inviting four foreign military personnel to apply for Canadian permanent residence — the smallest selection round in Express Entry history.

The draw required a minimum Comprehensive Ranking System score of 368, well below the 516 cut-off in the most recent Canadian Experience Class draw on July 21. Candidates needed to have created their Express Entry profiles before 8:11 p.m. UTC on June 2, 2026, according to CIC News.

A Category Born from Defence Strategy

The skilled military recruits category was introduced on February 18, 2026, when Immigration Minister Lena Metlege Diab announced a suite of new Express Entry priorities aligned with Prime Minister Mark Carney's defence and economic agenda.

"We are creating a new category for skilled military recruits to attract highly skilled foreign military applicants. Eligible recruits with a job offer from the Canadian Armed Forces, including doctors, nurses, and pilots, can be invited to apply for permanent residence."

— Lena Metlege Diab, Immigration Minister

The category sits within a broader $6.6 billion Defence Industrial Strategy that aims to prioritize domestic military procurement, grow Canada's defence industry revenues by 240%, and create up to 125,000 jobs over the next decade, according to Reuters.

Gen. Jenni Carignan, Canada's Chief of the Defence Staff, described the program as a way to spotlight specific capabilities the Canadian Armed Forces needs. "If you are a maritime technician operating somewhere, your file becomes very attractive as you're planning to move to Canada," Carignan said in February remarks.

Strict Eligibility Requirements

The program's narrow scope explains the tiny draw. Candidates must have a minimum of 10 years of continuous service in a recognized foreign military and hold a two-year post-secondary credential, whether Canadian or assessed through an Educational Credential Assessment.

A three-year, full-time job offer from the Canadian Armed Forces is required for specific pathways. The category targets F-35 fighter pilots, maritime technicians, military doctors and nurses, and specialists in cyber and space warfare, according to IRCC guidance reviewed by VisaVerge.

Canada is also prioritizing recruitment from NATO and Five Eyes partners — the United States, United Kingdom, Australia, and New Zealand — countries where interoperability and security vetting align with Canadian frameworks.

Express Entry in 2026: A Shifting Landscape

The military draw is the 42nd Express Entry round this year. IRCC has issued 104,616 invitations across all categories in 2026, with Canadian Experience Class draws accounting for 45,250 invitations and French-language proficiency draws issuing 40,500.

The broader pattern reflects Canada's pivot toward candidates already in the country or with specific in-demand skills. Provincial Nominee Program draws have accounted for 14 of the 42 rounds, while Canadian Experience Class draws make up 12 — together dominating the calendar.

Other targeted categories introduced this year include senior managers with Canadian work experience, transport workers such as pilots and aircraft mechanics, and physicians with Canadian experience.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For most Indian immigrants eyeing Canada, the military category won't apply directly — its requirements effectively limit eligibility to career military professionals from allied nations. But the draw illustrates Ottawa's growing willingness to use Express Entry's category-based selection to target highly specific workforce needs, a mechanism that could eventually expand to other sectors.

The Canadian Experience Class, which drew 2,000 invitations at a 516 CRS cut-off just two days before the military draw, remains the most active pathway for skilled workers already in Canada. Healthcare and trades categories continue to run regular rounds as well.

Candidates in the Express Entry pool can track upcoming draws and check their eligibility through IRCC's official notices, which are updated after each selection round.
